verses.text: On the third day, Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner courtyard of the palace, facing the king's hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the hall, facing the entrance.
When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard, he was pleased with her. He held out to her the gold scepter that was in his hand. So Esther came near and touched the tip of the scepter.
Then the king asked her, "What is it, Queen Esther? What do you want? I will give it to you, even up to half of my kingdom."
Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to a dinner I have prepared for the king."
The king said, "Bring Haman quickly, so we can do what Esther asks." So the king and Haman went to the dinner Esther had prepared.
While they were drinking wine, the king asked Esther again, "What do you want? It will be given to you. What is your request? Even up to half of my kingdom, it will be done."
Esther answered, "This is what I want and what I ask.

If the king is pleased with me, and if it pleases the king to give me what I want and do what I ask, let the king and Haman come tomorrow to the dinner I will prepare for them. Then I will answer the king's question."
Haman left that day happy and in high spirits. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and Mordecai did not stand up or show any fear of him, Haman was filled with anger against Mordecai.
But Haman controlled himself and went home. He called together his friends and his wife Zeresh.

Haman bragged to them about how rich he was and how many sons he had. He told them all the ways the king had honored him and how he had been promoted above the other officials and servants of the king.
Haman added, "And that's not all. Queen Esther invited no one but me to come with the king to the dinner she gave. And she has invited me again tomorrow with the king.
But none of this makes me happy as long as I see that Jew Mordecai sitting at the king's gate."

Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a pole set up, twenty-three meters high. In the morning, ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go with the king to the dinner and be happy." Haman liked the idea, and he had the pole set up.
